description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; found by the #1737
probe table, not caused by it.

perl's `sv_derived_from` resolves a NON-REF invocant through `gv_stashsv(sv, 0)`
-- WITHOUT GV_ADD -- so a class name whose stash does not exist is not derived
from anything, not even itself:

    $ perl -e 'no warnings; printf "[%s]\n", UNIVERSAL::isa("Nosuch","Nosuch")'
    []
    $ perl -e 'package Nosuch; sub x {} package main;
               printf "[%s]\n", UNIVERSAL::isa("Nosuch","Nosuch")'
    [1]

PCL answers 1 in BOTH cases: `%pcl-isa-ancestry` starts from the name and
always includes the name itself, so the stash question is never asked.
Probed on both trees.

WHERE: `p-isa` -> `%pcl-isa-ancestry` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.  The cheap
version is one `%pcl-find-package` (the stash table the dispatch already uses)
before the ancestry walk, for a non-ref invocant only.

THE CASE THAT WOULD BREAK IT, and why this was not fixed in s473t5f: a class
can exist in perl WITHOUT a sub -- `@splatt::ISA = 'zlopp'` makes the splatt
stash, and t/uni/universal.t's last four rows (`ok (splatt->isa('zlopp'))`,
`ok (!splatt->isa('plop'))`) are exactly that and PASS today.  So the stash
predicate must answer YES for a package created only by an @ISA assignment,
and that is a question about when PCL makes a CL package, not about isa.
Measure that first (does `@Foo::ISA = 'X'` with no `package Foo` create the
package?) -- the answer decides whether this is a two-line fix or a
representation question.

SIZE: not counted in any baseline row today (universal.t's 60 rows are #1736 +
#1737 + the residue named in the round record).  It is a correctness nit that
shows up when a program tests a class name it has not loaded -- which is
exactly what a `->can`/`->isa` feature probe does.
subject: UNIVERSAL::isa("Nosuch","Nosuch") is "" in perl (sv_derived_from wants the STASH to exist) and 1 in PCL -- %pcl-isa-ancestry never asks whether the class exists
